references.text: The Lord does not look at the things people look at. People look at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart. God's ability to know what is in people's hearts is reflected in Jesus' knowledge of all people [ref:1 Sam 16:7|1 Samuel 16:7].

David confesses that God searches him and knows him, knowing his words before they are on his tongue. This omniscience about humanity is reflected in Jesus' knowledge of all people in [ref:Sal 139:1-4|Psalm 139:1-4].

The heart is deceitful, and the Lord is the one who examines the heart and tests the kidneys. Jesus' knowledge of people's inner nature parallels this attribute of the Lord in [ref:Jer 17:9-10|Jeremiah 17:9-10].
The Lord, God of hosts, judges righteously and tests the kidneys and heart. Jesus' ability to know people reflects this divine attribute in [ref:Jer 11:20|Jeremiah 11:20].
Jesus did not need anyone to testify about humanity, for he himself knew what was in humanity. [ref:Joh 2:25|John 2:25] expands on and explains the reason why Jesus did not entrust himself to them.
Jesus knew from the beginning who did not believe and who would betray him. This confirms the same thing said here—that Jesus knew all people in [ref:Joh 6:64|John 6:64].
The disciples confess that Jesus knows all things and does not need anyone to ask him questions. This is a direct confirmation of the omniscience of Jesus described in [ref:Joh 16:30|John 16:30].
Peter says to Jesus, "Lord, you know all things; you know that I love you." Peter's confession underscores the omniscience about people that Jesus demonstrated in [ref:Joh 21:17|John 21:17].
Jesus knew their thoughts, which is a direct demonstration of his divine knowledge of people's inner lives, as described in [ref:Matt 9:4|Matthew 9:4].
In the prayer before casting lots, the apostles pray to the Lord who knows everyone's hearts. This knowledge of hearts points back to Jesus' knowledge of all people in [ref:Apg 1:24|Acts 1:24].

The exalted Christ says that he is the one who examines kidneys and hearts, and gives to each according to their deeds. This is the same divine knowledge of people's inner lives described in [ref:Åp 2:23|Revelation 2:23].
